svg.text: An object column: 2 x 32 tile cells in video RAM ($80 bytes)
byte offset of a cell = x * $40 + block * $10 + (row and 7) * 2
each cell: byte 0 = tile code bits 0-7
byte 1 = code bits 8-9 (bits 0-1), colour group (bits 2-5), flip x (6), flip y (7)

g.text: byte 0: 256 - y (the object's vertical position, negated)
byte 1: bits 7-5 = shape (PROM line), bits 4-0 = which column
byte 3: bits 3-0 = tile bank (x 1024 added to every code), bit 6 = x is negative

svg.text: The eight shapes (PROM lines $80-$F0, one entry per pair of rows)

g.text: $80 $90 $A0 $B0: skip rows 0-29, draw rows 30-31 from block 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 (a 2x2 sprite)
$C0 $D0: draw all 32 rows, blocks 0-3, reloading x from the entry (a full column)
$E0 $F0: the same, but x continues 16 pixels after the previous object (the playfield's 16 columns)
